newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- As the authorities closed the door on further talks with People Against Gangsterism and Drugs on Tuesday, the militant organisation vowed to continue its campaign to rid its community of these crimes.
- A renewed call has been made for an investigation into basic wages and conditions of employment in the gold mining industry.
- The equities and bond markets continued their free fall from late last week as traders took their lead from the U.S. markets' plunge and the futures close-out on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
- About one billion rand in Eurobond issues fall due in January, which could put pressure on the rand if investors take their losses and bail out of the rand.

- Transnet will be burdened with payments of two billion rand a year for the next nine years as a result of its underfunded pension and medical aid funds, raising questions about the future privatisation of the parastatal.
- A beer war appears to be brewing following an Advertising Standards Authority order for market leader SA Breweries to stop making "misleading" claims after complaints by rival Namibian Breweries.

- The international competitiveness of South Africa's gold mining industry remains hampered by a fragmented and inefficient labour process and a mining culture which has nurtured inefficient labour practices for the past 100 years, a recent study found.

- Deutsche Magnet Technik, which invested 210 million rand this year in South Africa's first ferrite magnet factory in KwaZulu Natal is planning to list on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in the first half of the year.

- Plans for the multi-million rand comeback to South Africa by Hertz, the U.S.-based car rental group which disenvested in 1987, have been hampered by the Airports company, which cannot supply kiosk space at the country's main airports.
- Police have called off talks with the Cape Town-based People Against Gangsterism and Drugs and promised to deal with the organisation with an iron fist.

- President Nelson Mandela is one of four African leaders who have been chosen by a summit of central African leaders to try to draw Zairian president Mobuto Sese Seko into negotiations to end the conflict in the Great Lakes region.
